title: Identification with the rational internal Hom and exceptional inverse image
statement:
In the rationalized constructible categories, the internal Hom
and exceptional inverse image agree with the operations defined
by coefficient passage in the manuscript. The integral tensor
product used for this passage is the completed derived tensor
product. In particular

$$
D_{X,E}K=R\mathcal Hom_E(K,\omega_{X,E}),
\qquad
Rf_E^!M\cong D_{X,E}f^*D_{Y,E}M
$$

for every separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$. The functor
$Rf_E^!$ is right adjoint to $Rf_{!,E}$ on these
constructible categories, and $\omega_{X,E}=Ra_{X,E}^!E$.
These identifications preserve evaluations, units, and counits,
including under finite scalar extension.

proof.text: Use the inherited global datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $\pi=\varpi_E$, $A_n=R/\pi^n$, and $\mathscr R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ on the small pro-etale site of $W$. In this proof an ambient integral tensor or internal Hom is over $\mathscr R_W$, not over the discrete constant sheaf $R_W$. Write $\mathcal C_R(W)=D^b_c(W,R)$ for the full derived-complete subcategory with constructible finite reductions and one uniform cohomological interval. Fix the small site skeletons and coefficient universes of the pro-etale site and size conventions, so the resolution and reflector lemmas apply. All inverse limits below use strict towers and their functorial derived-limit realization. These are the coefficient categories and operations appearing in the statement.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: coefficient and tensor conventions

proof.text: For $P,K\in\mathcal C_R(X)$ let $N=P\otimes^L_{\mathscr R_X}K$. Choose K-flat resolutions with flat terms. Their tensor is K-flat: tensor an acyclic complex first with one resolution and then with the other, obtaining an acyclic complex twice by the definition of K-flatness. The K-flat change-of-rings lemma makes their reductions K-flat with flat terms as well; the strict completed-tensor construction descends independently of these choices by integral-operations well-definedness. Reassociation of their ordinary tensor complexes, $(p\otimes k)\otimes a\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes(k\otimes a)$, identifies $N\otimes^L_{\mathscr R_X}(A_n)_X$ with $P_n\otimes^L_{A_n}K_n$. For $m\le n$, further reduction is $P_m\otimes^L_{A_m}K_m$; all transition cocycles hold already on these tensor representatives. Thus this is a normalized DVR tower. The residue-Tor lemma supplies uniform finite Tor intervals $[a,b]$, $[c,d]$ for the inputs, and finite tensor preservation supplies constructibility and interval $[a+c,b+d]$. Taking the degree-zero test module $(A_n)_X$ in the definition of Tor amplitude shows that this same interval contains the cohomological support of every tensor reduction: tensor with the coefficient unit is identified with the original complex by $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$, inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Normalized effectivity identifies the reductions of its derived limit with these objects and makes the limit complete. Hence $C(N):=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(P_n\otimes^L_{A_n}K_n)$ belongs to $\mathcal C_R(X)$. By the definition of integral operations this is precisely $P\widehat\otimes_R^LK$. No assertion of local perfection on the site is used.

source.place: Proof, paragraphs 1-2: completed tensor and uniform intervals

proof.text:
Here is the completion adjunction with its actual unit. The DVR $R$ is Noetherian, since every ideal is principal. Apply constant-completion equivalence with $A=R$, $I=(\pi)$, and completed coefficient sheaf $\mathscr R_X$. It identifies quotient-tower completion $C(N)=R\lim_n(N\otimes^L_{\mathscr R_X}(A_n)_X)$ with Koszul completion, respecting their specified units $\eta_N$. Apply the ringed-site Koszul reflector to $\mathcal O=\mathscr R_X$ and the single global section $\pi$. It gives a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C(N),M)\xrightarrow{\;\circ\eta_N\;}\operatorname{Hom}(N,M)$$
for every locally derived-complete $M$. An object of $\mathcal C_R(X)$ is isomorphic to its quotient-tower derived limit by the derived-completeness definition. That limit is locally complete by the reflector and the quotient/Koszul comparison; local completeness is invariant under isomorphism. Thus every such $M$ satisfies the reflector hypothesis, and its canonical reflector unit is an isomorphism. This uses neither Noetherianity of the sheaf $\mathscr R_X$ nor a chosen arbitrary lift to a Roos triangle as the completion unit.

source.place: Tags 099B (lemma-derived-completion) and 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul); quotient comparison Tag 099M in proetale.tex, with coefficient flatness Tag 093M in sites-modules.tex

proof.text:
The ambient tensor-Hom adjunction needed here is for an arbitrary ringed site. Choose K-flat representatives $Q_P,Q_K$ with flat terms and a K-injective representative $I_M$. The internal Hom complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(Q_K,I_M)$ is K-injective. The functorial total-complex currying isomorphism gives
$$\mathcal Hom^\bullet(Q_P,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(Q_K,I_M))\cong\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\operatorname{Tot}(Q_P\otimes Q_K),I_M).$$
These represent the corresponding derived internal Homs: the definition computes internal Hom into a K-injective resolution, and the cited quasi-isomorphism invariance permits the K-flat replacements. Taking degree-zero derived global sections and using the global-sections/Hom identification yields
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes^L_{\mathscr R_X}K,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathscr R_X}(K,M)).$$
The currying formula sends a map $h$ to $p\mapsto(k\mapsto h(p\otimes k))$, where, for $p\in Q_P^i$, the tensor differential is $d(p\otimes k)=dp\otimes k+(-1)^ip\otimes dk$ and the differential of a homogeneous Hom map $h$ of degree $t$ is $dh=d_Mh-(-1)^thd$. Substitution in these two formulas verifies that currying commutes with the differential, with no additional sign in the displayed currying formula. Its inverse evaluates. This describes the evaluation and the naturality of the adjunction, rather than invoking a tensor-Hom theorem for scheme structure sheaves.

source.place: Tags 0A90 (lemma-compose), 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined), 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U), and the proof of lemma-internal-hom immediately following 08JA

proof.text:
For $P,K,M\in\mathcal C_R(X)$, integral internal Hom is in $\mathcal C_R(X)$ by the integral-Hom preservation statement. Combine Steps 2-4, using fullness of this subcategory, to obtain the natural $R$-linear bijection
$$\Phi_R:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_R}(P\widehat\otimes_R^LK,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_R}(P,R\mathcal Hom_R(K,M)).$$
Its left-to-right map is first precomposition with the canonical completion unit, then currying. The counit is the unique map $R\mathcal Hom_R(K,M)\widehat\otimes_R^LK\to M$ whose precomposition with that unit is ambient evaluation. The unit is $\Phi_R(1_{P\widehat\otimes_R^LK}):P\to R\mathcal Hom_R(K,P\widehat\otimes_R^LK)$; the counit is $\Phi_R^{-1}(1_{R\mathcal Hom_R(K,M)})$. Naturality of $\Phi_R$ makes the two triangle identities the assertion that currying and uncurrying are inverse. Thus completion has not silently changed the tensor adjunction or its evaluation.

source.place: Proof, paragraphs 3-5: apply the completion adjunction to the ambient tensor-Hom adjunction

proof.text:
The raw scalar localization has exactly the same objects and Hom groups $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_R}(U,V)\otimes_RE$. Tensoring $\Phi_R$ with $E$ therefore gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_c(X,E)}(P\otimes_E^LK,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_c(X,E)}(P,R\mathcal Hom_E(K,M)).$$
Every map is a finite sum of integral maps times scalars; the displayed bijection sends $h\otimes a$ to $\Phi_R(h)\otimes a$. Its naturality for fractions follows from $R$-linearity: the two sides of each integral naturality identity are multiplied by the same product of the denominators' inverses. In two-variable operations $u\otimes a$ and $v\otimes b$ act by the integral operation on $(u,v)$ times $ab$ (precomposition in the contravariant variable). Thus these are exactly the coefficient-passage functors, on maps as well as objects. The evaluation, unit, counit and their identities are the integral ones tensored with $1$, as follows by applying this Hom bijection to identities. No new objects from a Karoubi envelope are involved.

source.place: Proof, paragraphs 5-6: scalar-localized Hom bijection and its evaluation

proof.text: Integral Verdier duality is $D_{X,R}K=R\mathcal Hom_R(K,\omega_{X,R})$ and the rational duality functor is its localization, with $\omega_{X,E}$ the image of $\omega_{X,R}$. Specialize Step 6 to that second argument. It gives the asserted equality $D_{X,E}K=R\mathcal Hom_E(K,\omega_{X,E})$, with evaluation the rationalized integral evaluation. The double-dual map is the same one as in rational Verdier duality, since both are obtained by transposing that evaluation; the cited integral and rational duality statements identify these actual maps.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 6: specialize internal Hom to the dualizing object

proof.text: For separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$, put $A_R=Rf_{!,R}$ and $G_R(M)=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n Rf_n^!M_n$. The integral exceptional-adjoint theorem supplies the adjunction $A_R\dashv G_R$ on the stated bounded constructible categories, its actual unit $\eta_R$, counit $\varepsilon_R$, and the canonical isomorphism $G_R\cong D_{X,R}f^*_{\mathrm{comp}}D_{Y,R}$ identifying those data. The compact-support functor is $R$-linear by its coefficient-level construction and strict derived limit. The displayed formula for $G_R$ also makes it $R$-linear: internal duality acts by linear precomposition (Steps 4 and 7), completed pullback is linear on the coefficient representatives of Step 1, and the formula contains two dualities. For $h:A_RK\to M$, its adjoint is $G_R(h)\circ\eta_{R,K}$, so the adjoint of $ah$ is $G_R(ah)\circ\eta_{R,K}=a(G_R(h)\circ\eta_{R,K})$. This proves the required linearity of the actual adjunction bijection. Apply scalar transport to the functors and natural transformations, and explicitly tensor the integral Hom bijection with $E$. This gives $A_E\dashv G_E$, with units $\eta_R\otimes1$ and counits $\varepsilon_R\otimes1$; the triangle equations remain equations after tensoring with $1$. The transport statement alone is not being used as a theorem asserting that every adjunction survives an unspecified localization.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 7: localize the integral exceptional adjunction

proof.text: The left adjoint $A_E$ of Step 8 is the rational compact-support functor: its integral representative and strict finite-reduction tower are exactly the ones in the definition of rational compact support. Likewise $G_E$ is the rationalized finite-stage exceptional inverse image specified in the exceptional-inverse-image definition. Localizing the integral formula, using the already identified pullback and duality functors, gives $Rf_E^!M\cong D_{X,E}f^*D_{Y,E}M$. If either operation is instead characterized by the adjunction, its comparison is forced by the counit: the unique map between right adjoints whose transpose is the other counit is inverse to the reverse comparison, since both composites transpose to the original counit. This proves preservation of the units and counits too. For $f=a_X$, the integral theorem identifies $G_R(R)$ with $\omega_{X,R}$, so rationalizing gives $Ra_{X,E}^!E=\omega_{X,E}$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 7: identify the prescribed operations, formula and structure-morphism value

proof.text: We now check finite extension, including the adjunction maps. Let $E\subset L$, $S=\mathcal O_L$, $v=\varpi_L$, ramification index $e$, and $r=[L:E]$. At level $n$ use $B_n=S/\pi^nS=S/v^{en}$, finite free over $A_n$; these are the specified cofinal $S$-levels. Write $T_W$ for integral completed extension. Finite-free completed-scalar comparison identifies it, by its canonical completion map, with ordinary derived extension $-\otimes^L_{\mathscr R_W}\mathscr S_W$, where $\mathscr S_W$ is finite free of rank $r$ over $\mathscr R_W$. This comparison is between the actual strict-tower functors, not just unrelated objects with isomorphic reductions. The integral dualizing, internal-Hom and duality comparisons $u,v_{K,M},\beta$ preserve evaluation and biduality; pullback and tensor also have the stated scalar comparisons. In particular internal-Hom evaluation has the scalar rule $(h\otimes s,k\otimes t)\mapsto h(k)\otimes st$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 8: use finite free extension, not arbitrary infinite coefficient extension

proof.text:
Fix one compactification $f=pj$ at all coefficient levels. The compact-support reduction-tower functor gives a lift to the derived category of strict towers, whose evaluations and quotient transitions are exactly the stated finite compact-support functors; use this lift when applying derived inverse limit below. At $A_n\to B_n$, extension by zero commutes with finite direct sums and restriction of scalars because it is an exact additive left adjoint computed degreewise. The $Rp_*$ finite-free comparison is the one in the finite-free-extension statement, and composing gives $T_{Y,n}Rf_{!,A_n}\cong Rf_{!,B_n}T_{X,n}$. These maps are compatible with the quotient transitions: restriction of scalars commutes with $Rf_!$, and the cited finite-free comparisons commute with reductions. Choose an $R$-basis of $S$, giving a compatible basis of every $B_n$. On the underlying $A_n$-complexes the comparison is the finite-sum map $(Rf_{!,A_n}K_n)^{\oplus r}\to Rf_{!,A_n}(K_n^{\oplus r})$. A basis change acts by the same matrix on both sides, so the map is independent of the basis. Finite sums commute with termwise products and $1-s$ and hence with the strict-tower cone computing $R\lim$; exact countable products justify this model on pro-etale modules. Taking these actual tower maps and the cofinal levels of Step 10 yields
$$\alpha:T_Y A_R\xrightarrow{\sim}A_S T_X.$$
Its underlying map in any basis is finite-sum distributivity. All its inverses and compositions are therefore compatible with the chosen reduction maps, not just identifiable after reduction.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 8, expanded: finite-free compact-support comparison on strict coefficient towers

proof.text:
Let $U_W$ be restriction from $\mathscr S_W$ to $\mathscr R_W$; it leaves underlying abelian sheaves unchanged and is exact. The balanced maps $h\mapsto[k\mapsto h(1\otimes k)]$ and $g\mapsto[s\otimes k\mapsto s g(k)]$ give $T_W\dashv U_W$ on module sheaves. Finite freeness makes $T_W$ exact as well. Thus the partial-derived-adjunction lemma applies with everywhere-defined derived functors: their quasi-isomorphism diagrams are already constant up to the invertible images of the quasi-isomorphisms. It gives the same adjunction on ambient derived categories. It restricts to the constructible categories. Indeed $T_W$ preserves them by the integral finite-extension statement. For $N\in\mathcal C_S(W)$, choose an $S$-K-flat resolution; it is also $R$-K-flat: for an acyclic $R$-complex $Q$, first tensor with the finite free $\mathscr S_W$, then with the $S$-K-flat resolution. Both operations preserve the required acyclicity. Tensoring this representative gives
$$(U_WN)\otimes^L_{\mathscr R_W}(A_n)_W=\operatorname{Res}_{A_n\to B_n}(N\otimes^L_{\mathscr S_W}(B_n)_W).$$
Restriction preserves finite-level constructibility (finite modules remain finite, and the same local constant presentations apply) and the given uniform cohomological interval. It also commutes with products and cones on the underlying sheaves. Completeness therefore follows from the complete $S$-tower on the cofinal $en$ levels of Step 10. Hence $U_WN\in\mathcal C_R(W)$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 8, expanded using Tag 0DVC (derived-lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors): finite-free extension/restriction adjunction and its domain

proof.text:
Apply Steps 8 and 12 over both rings. For $N\in\mathcal C_S(Y)$ the following natural bijections, in this order, determine an isomorphism $\rho:U_XG_SN\cong G_RU_YN$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,U_XG_SN)&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(T_XK,G_SN)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(A_ST_XK,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(T_YA_RK,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(A_RK,U_YN)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,G_RU_YN).
\end{aligned}$$
The middle map is precomposition with $\alpha_K$. Taking identities on the two representing objects gives inverse comparison maps: their composites are identities because the displayed bijections are inverse and natural. In particular this uses only the constructible exceptional adjunction, not an unbounded ambient pro-etale exceptional adjoint.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 8, expanded: explicit Hom bijections defining the right-adjoint comparison

proof.text:
Define $b_M:T_XG_RM\to G_ST_YM$ as the transpose under $A_S\dashv G_S$ of
$$A_ST_XG_RM\xrightarrow{\alpha_{G_RM}^{-1}}T_YA_RG_RM\xrightarrow{T_Y\varepsilon_{R,M}}T_YM.$$
This map is invertible. To check it, choose the basis of Step 11. Then $U_YT_YM=M^{\oplus r}$, and $\rho$ of Step 13 identifies the underlying target with $G_R(M^{\oplus r})$. A right adjoint preserves finite products; here they are finite biproducts. The $i$-th component of $\rho U_Xb_M$ is $G_R$ applied to the $i$-th coefficient projection, composed with the map transposed from the corresponding component of $T_Y\varepsilon_R$. By the scalar rule for the extension/restriction adjunction and the finite-sum description of $\alpha$, this is projection onto the $i$-th copy of $G_RM$, followed by $G_R\varepsilon_R\circ\eta_RG_R=1$. The off-diagonal components are zero. Thus the underlying matrix of $b_M$ is the identity on $(G_RM)^{\oplus r}$. Restriction detects an isomorphism, since it leaves the cohomology sheaves of its cone unchanged. This proves invertibility without inferring equality of maps from equality of their finite reductions.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 8, expanded: finite-free mate isomorphism; finite products from Tag 0038 (categories-lemma-adjoint-exact)

proof.text:
The maps just constructed identify the actual adjunction data. By definition of transpose,
$$\varepsilon_{S,T_YM}\circ A_S(b_M)\circ\alpha_{G_RM}=T_Y(\varepsilon_{R,M}).$$
The unit identity is
$$b_{A_RK}\circ T_X(\eta_{R,K})=G_S(\alpha_K^{-1})\circ\eta_{S,T_XK}.$$
For verification, transpose both sides under $A_S\dashv G_S$. The left side becomes $T_Y\varepsilon_{R,A_RK}\circ\alpha_{G_RA_RK}^{-1}\circ A_ST_X\eta_{R,K}$. Naturality of $\alpha$ moves the last factor past $\alpha^{-1}$, after which $\varepsilon_RA_R\circ A_R\eta_R=1$ reduces it to $\alpha_K^{-1}$. The right side has the same transpose by the other triangle identity. These formulas also describe the finite-level mate on $A_n\to B_n$. The compact-support tower maps of Step 11, the finite quotient compatibility of the duality comparisons, and the integral theorem's identification of the canonical units and counits identify the same formulas for the functor $G_R=R\lim\operatorname{Res}_nRf_n^!$. Thus $b$ is its coefficient-passage comparison. Write $c_Z:T_Xf_R^*Z\xrightarrow{\sim}f_S^*T_YZ$ for the supplied completed-pullback comparison, and $\beta^W_Z:T_WD_{W,R}Z\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{W,S}T_WZ$ for the supplied duality comparison. The comparison on the duality formula is the following specific composite:
$$\begin{aligned}
T_XD_{X,R}f_R^*D_{Y,R}M
&\xrightarrow{\beta^X_{f_R^*D_{Y,R}M}}D_{X,S}T_Xf_R^*D_{Y,R}M\\
&\xrightarrow{D_{X,S}(c_{D_{Y,R}M}^{-1}\circ f_S^*((\beta^Y_M)^{-1}))}D_{X,S}f_S^*D_{Y,S}T_YM.
\end{aligned}$$
The inverse comparisons inside $D_{X,S}$ are required by contravariance: their composite has source $f_S^*D_{Y,S}T_YM$ and target $T_Xf_R^*D_{Y,R}M$. Use the integral exceptional theorem's canonical formula identifications at source and target to view this as a map $b'_M:T_XG_RM\to G_ST_YM$. Transpose $b'_M$ through $A_S\dashv G_S$. The two Hom comparisons for internal duality replace each evaluation by $(h\otimes s,k\otimes t)\mapsto h(k)\otimes st$, and the integral identification carries its final counit to $\varepsilon_R$. Its transpose is therefore $T_Y\varepsilon_R\circ\alpha^{-1}$, the defining transpose of $b$; injectivity of the adjunction bijection identifies the maps. This explains where both the evaluation and the counit compatibilities, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism of functors, enter.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 8, expanded: mate equations for units and counits and the duality formula

proof.text: Finally rationalize the finite-extension comparisons. By the definition of $-\otimes_E L$, its integral representative is exactly $T$, and each component of $\alpha,b,u,v,\beta$ is sent to that component tensored with $1$. Composition in raw scalar localization is bilinear, so both equations of Step 15 and the evaluation identities remain the same equations after localization. Coherence for $E\subset L\subset L'$ follows at compact support from multiplication $(k\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto k\otimes st$ on the finite free tower maps; taking mates gives the same equality for $b$ because their transposes are the same composite counit. For internal Hom and duality, identity and associator coherence are those of the integral comparisons. The rational duality theorem gives the corresponding evaluation and biduality comparisons as well. This proves every scalar-extension compatibility claimed in the item within the specified rationalized constructible categories.
